# Open Cannabis Research Initiative

> Independent patient-led research advocacy. Proposed studies are not active trials; literature metadata is provisional and should be checked against original sources.

## Proposed clinical case report | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/case-report.html

Proposed clinical case report
Proposed — seeking clinical collaboration. A clinician suggested that patient-reported treatment observations may warrant a case report. No report has been completed or accepted.
Purpose
Document treatment chronology, formulation information where available, symptom changes, adverse effects and alternative explanations. A case report cannot establish causation.
Clinical oversight
A qualified clinician would assess suitability, obtain consent, protect privacy and follow journal and institutional requirements. No personal medical records are solicited through this site. Discuss clinical collaboration
Research advocacy only. Cannabis is not an established PTSD treatment; discuss care with a qualified clinician.

## Partnership charter | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/charter.html

Partnership charter
Partnership principles
Participation is voluntary and nonexclusive. Institutions retain scientific independence, responsibility for ethics and regulatory compliance, and control over data and intellectual property subject to applicable agreements. Sponsors should not control interpretation or suppress publication. Positive, negative and inconclusive findings are welcome.
Open science
Encourage preregistration, shared outcome definitions, independent replication, transparent funding disclosures and open-access publication where feasible. Share protocols and aggregate results where permitted; participant data require consent and appropriate governance. Investigators may use Open Science Framework and applicable trial registries. No registry or formal consortium is currently established.
Research accessibility and clinical education
Encourage lawful access to standardized research materials for qualified investigators, nonexclusive institutional funding, publication of adverse and inconclusive findings, accessible protocols and literature, clinically useful formulation comparisons and patient participation in identifying research questions. Clearly distinguish established evidence from preliminary findings and speculation. Evidence summaries should support shared decision-making, not replace clinical care.
Research advocacy only. Cannabis is not an established PTSD treatment; discuss care with a qualified clinician.

## Get involved | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/contact.html

Get involved
Help expand independent cannabis research and improve evidence for patient and clinician decisions.
Principal investigators, clinicians, analytical scientists, pharmaceutical developers and institutional research sponsors are invited to get in touch. Email me to discuss collaboration, recommend additional research or suggest new research questions. Please include your institutional affiliation, relevant expertise and proposed area of collaboration, if applicable. Email me
This initiative does not provide treatment, products, clinical enrollment or medical advice.
Contribute an independent study
Institutions are welcome to propose original investigations, replication studies, multisite collaborations or complementary analyses. Please indicate your research interests and whether you would prefer independent or coordinated participation.
Research advocacy only. Cannabis is not an established PTSD treatment; discuss care with a qualified clinician.

## A clearer path to trauma recovery | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/

Patient-led translational research initiative
Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Independent science. Informed patients. Educated clinical decisions.
Advancing independent cannabis research to help patients and clinicians understand benefits, risks and uncertainties. Explore research objectivesPartner with us
Our mission
Cannabis research remains fragmented, with important gaps in evidence for clinical and patient decision-making. The Open Cannabis Research Initiative seeks to expand independent, accessible and scientifically rigorous investigation of cannabinoids, terpenes, formulation chemistry, therapeutic applications, adverse effects and long-term outcomes.
Our objective is not to promote consumption or establish predetermined conclusions, but to empower patients and clinicians with evidence for informed, individualized decisions. PTSD is our initial research priority, not the limit of our scientific interests.
Flagship research program: PTSD
We propose a systematic investigation of chemically characterized cannabinoid formulations, using terpene-free THC as a reference condition. The central hypothesis is that formulation composition may influence tolerability and PTSD-related outcomes, including whether sustained nightmare relief facilitates trauma processing.
This is an investigator-seeking initiative, not an active clinical trial. Patient observations are hypothesis-generating, not evidence of efficacy.
PTSD research priorities
Nightmares and sleep
Study dream recall, sleep quality and trauma-related nightmares. Learn more
Individual terpenes
Isolate the effects of each compound rather than relying on strain labels. Learn more
Functional impairment
Measure cognition, alertness and daily functioning. Learn more
Long-term recovery
Distinguish temporary relief from sustained improvement. Learn more
Scientific evidence
Separate human trials from preliminary findings. Learn more
Collaboration
Invite independent academic and industry support. Learn moreMore research priorities
A distributed research initiative
We invite multiple independent institutions to investigate shared research questions, replicate findings and contribute complementary studies. No single institution or sponsor is intended to control the research agenda. Coordinated protocols and independent replication can strengthen the reliability and generalizability of findings. Explore institutional collaboration
Research prospectus · Partnership charter
Beyond PTSD
Explore cannabinoid pharmacology, drug interactions, formulation standardization, long-term outcomes and clinical education. Explore the broader research agenda
Research advocacy only. Cannabis is not an established PTSD treatment; discuss care with a qualified clinician.

Bonn-Miller et al. Human randomized trial PTSD; THC; CBD; no superiority over placebo in primary comparison 10.1371/journal.pone.0246990
University of Pennsylvania; Scottsdale Research Institute; MAPS; University of Colorado; VA San Diego; UC San Diego
80 randomized at stage 1; no significant superiority over placebo on primary PTSD outcome.

Jetly et al. Human randomized trial PTSD; nightmares; nabilone; small sample 10.1016/j.psyneuen.2014.11.002

Read the partnership charter · Research prospectus
Academic investigators
Academic cannabinoid laboratories, PTSD clinicians, sleep researchers, analytical laboratories, pharmaceutical developers and nonprofit research sponsors are invited to explore the research questions.
We seek principal investigators with expertise in cannabinoid pharmacology, psychiatry, sleep medicine, clinical trial design and biostatistics to refine hypotheses and assess feasibility.
Industry research and development partners
Potential contributions include institutional funding, analytical chemistry, toxicology and standardized formulation expertise. No endorsement, affiliation or funding commitment is claimed.
Collaboration opportunities
Investigator-sponsored research funding and grant development
Institutional analytical chemistry and formulation characterization
Pharmacokinetic, toxicological and delivery-system expertise
Independent evidence synthesis and protocol development
No materials are requested for personal use. Any study materials would be handled by authorized research institutions.
Independence
Disclose conflicts of interest and protect independent study design, analysis and publication. Discuss a research partnership
Open participation across institutions
Participation is nonexclusive. Universities, hospitals, independent laboratories and industry research teams are invited to contribute parallel studies, independent replications or complementary research. Multiple sponsors may support distinct institutional projects without controlling publication or interpretation.
We encourage collaboration on common measurement standards, protocol development, reference formulation characterization and evidence synthesis while preserving each institution's independence. Participation does not require affiliation with another participating institution.
The initiative seeks to connect investigators; it does not currently claim an established consortium or confirmed institutional membership.
Research accessibility and clinical education
Encourage lawful access to standardized research materials for qualified investigators, nonexclusive institutional funding, publication of adverse and inconclusive findings, accessible protocols and literature, clinically useful formulation comparisons and patient participation in identifying research questions. Clearly distinguish established evidence from preliminary findings and speculation. Evidence summaries should support shared decision-making, not replace clinical care.
Research advocacy only. Cannabis is not an established PTSD treatment; discuss care with a qualified clinician.

## Patient perspective | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/perspective.html

Patient perspective
A patient-led hypothesis, not clinical evidence.
Clinical rationale and patient-reported observations
Patient observations motivate investigation of whether sustained relief from distressing dreams can create psychological space for trauma processing. The initiative also asks whether removing or selectively reintroducing terpenes changes tolerability.
Research should distinguish symptomatic relief from durable improvement, using validated PTSD measures and longitudinal follow-up. The proposed mechanism remains untested.
Dream recall is not the same as REM sleep or the absence of dreaming. Individual experiences cannot establish causation or general effectiveness.
Research advocacy only. Cannabis is not an established PTSD treatment; discuss care with a qualified clinician.

## Treatment discontinuation | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/project-discontinuation.html

Treatment discontinuation
Proposed project — seeking independent investigators.
Research question
What happens to sleep and symptoms after treatment ends?
Scientific rationale
Patient observations and gaps in existing evidence motivate this hypothesis; efficacy is not established. Review relevant literature.
Proposed methodology
Clinician-supervised observational follow-up or ethically approved discontinuation designs.
Candidate outcomes and limitations
Withdrawal, tolerance, nightmare recurrence and durable improvement.
Collaboration
Multiple institutions may pursue parallel or complementary studies. Investigators determine sample size, endpoints, approvals and analysis plans independently. Propose an independent study
All research projects
Research advocacy only. Cannabis is not an established PTSD treatment; discuss care with a qualified clinician.

## Formulation comparison | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/project-formulations.html

Formulation comparison
Proposed project — seeking independent investigators.
Research question
Does chemical composition predict response better than strain labels?
Scientific rationale
Patient observations and gaps in existing evidence motivate this hypothesis; efficacy is not established. Review relevant literature.
Proposed methodology
Compare analytically characterized formulations with matched cannabinoid exposure under approved protocols.
Candidate outcomes and limitations
Tolerability, pharmacokinetics and symptom outcomes.
Collaboration
Multiple institutions may pursue parallel or complementary studies. Investigators determine sample size, endpoints, approvals and analysis plans independently. Propose an independent study
All research projects

## Nightmares and sleep | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/project-nightmares.html

Nightmares and sleep
Proposed project — seeking independent investigators.
Research question
Does formulation affect trauma-related nightmares or dream recall?
Scientific rationale
Patient observations and gaps in existing evidence motivate this hypothesis; efficacy is not established. Review relevant literature.
Proposed methodology
Clinician-designed feasibility studies with sleep diaries and polysomnography where appropriate.
Candidate outcomes and limitations
Nightmare frequency, sleep quality and REM architecture; distinguish recall from dreaming.
Collaboration
Multiple institutions may pursue parallel or complementary studies. Investigators determine sample size, endpoints, approvals and analysis plans independently. Propose an independent study
All research projects
Research advocacy only. Cannabis is not an established PTSD treatment; discuss care with a qualified clinician.

## Longitudinal trauma recovery | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/project-recovery.html

Longitudinal trauma recovery
Proposed project — seeking independent investigators.
Research question
Is sustained nightmare relief associated with durable recovery?
Scientific rationale
Patient observations and gaps in existing evidence motivate this hypothesis; efficacy is not established. Review relevant literature.
Proposed methodology
Prospective follow-up with appropriate comparison groups and documentation of concurrent therapy.
Candidate outcomes and limitations
CAPS-5, PCL-5, functioning and persistence of change; confounding and attrition.
Collaboration
Multiple institutions may pursue parallel or complementary studies. Investigators determine sample size, endpoints, approvals and analysis plans independently. Propose an independent study
All research projects

## Selective terpene reintroduction | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/project-reintroduction.html

Selective terpene reintroduction
Proposed project — seeking independent investigators.
Research question
Can individual compounds modify tolerability without worsening other outcomes?
Scientific rationale
Patient observations and gaps in existing evidence motivate this hypothesis; efficacy is not established. Review relevant literature.
Proposed methodology
Prioritize candidates using existing human evidence and toxicology; independent controlled comparisons.
Candidate outcomes and limitations
Anxiety, impairment and adverse effects; PTSD outcomes require separate validation.
Collaboration
Multiple institutions may pursue parallel or complementary studies. Investigators determine sample size, endpoints, approvals and analysis plans independently. Propose an independent study
All research projects

## Terpene interaction screening | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/project-terpene-screening.html

Terpene interaction screening
Proposed project — seeking independent investigators.
Research question
Do individual terpenes alter acute THC effects?
Scientific rationale
Patient observations and gaps in existing evidence motivate this hypothesis; efficacy is not established. Review relevant literature.
Proposed methodology
Controlled interaction studies after toxicology review; matched exposure, placebo and terpene-only controls.
Candidate outcomes and limitations
Anxiety, paranoia, adverse events; independent replication.
Collaboration
Multiple institutions may pursue parallel or complementary studies. Investigators determine sample size, endpoints, approvals and analysis plans independently. Propose an independent study
All research projects
Research advocacy only. Cannabis is not an established PTSD treatment; discuss care with a qualified clinician.

## Research prospectus | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/prospectus.html

Research prospectus
Institutional discussion document — proposed research, not an approved protocol.
Our mission
Cannabis research remains fragmented, with important gaps in evidence for clinical and patient decision-making. The Open Cannabis Research Initiative seeks to expand independent, accessible and scientifically rigorous investigation of cannabinoids, terpenes, formulation chemistry, therapeutic applications, adverse effects and long-term outcomes.
Our objective is not to promote consumption or establish predetermined conclusions, but to empower patients and clinicians with evidence for informed, individualized decisions. PTSD is our initial research priority, not the limit of our scientific interests.
Flagship program rationale: PTSD
Investigate whether chemically characterized cannabinoid formulations differ in PTSD-related sleep symptoms, anxiety and functional impairment. Patient observations generate hypotheses, not proof of efficacy.
Research portfolio
Terpene interaction screening: Do individual terpenes alter acute THC effects?
Nightmares and sleep: Does formulation affect trauma-related nightmares or dream recall?
Longitudinal trauma recovery: Is sustained nightmare relief associated with durable recovery?
Functional impairment: Do formulations differ in cognitive and psychomotor effects?
Formulation comparison: Does chemical composition predict response better than strain labels?
Selective terpene reintroduction: Can individual compounds modify tolerability without worsening other outcomes?
Treatment discontinuation: What happens to sleep and symptoms after treatment ends?
Broader research agenda
Cannabinoid pharmacology
Individual cannabinoids and interactions.
Terpene pharmacology
Compound-specific effects.
Formulation chemistry
Chemical composition rather than strain labels.
Drug interactions
Interactions with prescription medications.
Individual variability
Differences in patient response.
Long-term outcomes
Benefits, harms, tolerance and dependence.
Delivery methods
Absorption, effectiveness and adverse effects.
Functional impairment
Cognition and everyday functioning.
Therapeutic applications
Condition-specific clinical outcomes.
Product standardization
Consistency and reproducibility.
Research accessibility
Access to standardized materials for qualified investigators.
Clinical education
Accessible evidence summaries for patients and clinicians.
These are proposed research directions, not active studies or clinical recommendations.
Institutional model
Independent parallel studies, replication and multisite collaboration with shared measures where appropriate. Sponsors may support institutional research without controlling findings.
Partnership principles
Participation is voluntary and nonexclusive. Institutions retain scientific independence, responsibility for ethics and regulatory compliance, and control over data and intellectual property subject to applicable agreements. Sponsors should not control interpretation or suppress publication. Positive, negative and inconclusive findings are welcome.
Open science
Encourage preregistration, shared outcome definitions, independent replication, transparent funding disclosures and open-access publication where feasible. Share protocols and aggregate results where permitted; participant data require consent and appropriate governance. Investigators may use Open Science Framework and applicable trial registries. No registry or formal consortium is currently established.
Research accessibility and clinical education
Encourage lawful access to standardized research materials for qualified investigators, nonexclusive institutional funding, publication of adverse and inconclusive findings, accessible protocols and literature, clinically useful formulation comparisons and patient participation in identifying research questions. Clearly distinguish established evidence from preliminary findings and speculation. Evidence summaries should support shared decision-making, not replace clinical care.
Next steps
Identify qualified investigators, review evidence and feasibility, develop protocols and secure ethics and regulatory approvals before any enrollment. Discuss partnershipDownload prospectus (HTML)Open print-friendly prospectus
The downloadable document works offline and can be circulated by email or printed using your browser.
Research advocacy only. Cannabis is not an established PTSD treatment; discuss care with a qualified clinician.

## Research proposals | Open Cannabis Research Initiative
Source: https://opencannabisresearchinitiative.org/research.html

Research agenda
Our mission
Cannabis research remains fragmented, with important gaps in evidence for clinical and patient decision-making. The Open Cannabis Research Initiative seeks to expand independent, accessible and scientifically rigorous investigation of cannabinoids, terpenes, formulation chemistry, therapeutic applications, adverse effects and long-term outcomes.
Our objective is not to promote consumption or establish predetermined conclusions, but to empower patients and clinicians with evidence for informed, individualized decisions. PTSD is our initial research priority, not the limit of our scientific interests.
A staged, independently supervised research program.
Flagship program: PTSD research projects
Terpene interaction screening
Do individual terpenes alter acute THC effects? View proposal
Nightmares and sleep
Does formulation affect trauma-related nightmares or dream recall? View proposal
Longitudinal trauma recovery
Is sustained nightmare relief associated with durable recovery? View proposal
Functional impairment
Do formulations differ in cognitive and psychomotor effects? View proposal
Formulation comparison
Does chemical composition predict response better than strain labels? View proposal
Selective terpene reintroduction
Can individual compounds modify tolerability without worsening other outcomes? View proposal
Treatment discontinuation
What happens to sleep and symptoms after treatment ends? View proposal
Proposed clinical case report · Open-science framework
Research questions
Does individual terpene composition alter acute anxiety or functional impairment at matched THC exposure?
Do formulations differ in trauma-related nightmares, flashbacks or sleep architecture?
Is sustained nightmare relief associated with improved trauma processing and durable clinical outcomes?
Study design
Begin with analytical characterization and toxicology review. Qualified investigators would design randomized, blinded comparisons of purified THC, placebo, terpene-only controls, individual terpene–THC combinations and characterized mixtures, with matched THC exposure.
Outcomes
Anxiety, paranoia, flashback frequency and severity
Nightmares, dream recall, sleep quality and sleep architecture
Attention, memory, psychomotor performance and daily functioning
Longitudinal PTSD severity, trauma processing and persistence of improvement
Adverse events, tolerance, dependence and discontinuation effects
Proposed work packages
Systematic evidence mapping and analytical characterization.
Preclinical safety and pharmacology assessment where justified.
Investigator-designed controlled human interaction studies.
PTSD-specific feasibility and longitudinal efficacy studies, subject to prior safety findings.
Candidate measures include CAPS-5, PCL-5, sleep diaries, polysomnography and validated cognitive tasks. Investigators would determine eligibility, sample size, endpoints and statistical analysis before enrollment.
Safeguards
Ethics approval, informed consent, medical oversight, preregistration, independent analysis and publication rights are essential. No self-experimentation or recruitment is conducted here.
Multi-institutional research and independent replication
Encourage multiple institutions to investigate the same terpene–THC interactions and PTSD outcomes through independently conducted studies. Complementary studies may investigate alternative formulations, populations, delivery methods and longitudinal outcomes.
Independent replication using comparable protocols, reference formulations and endpoints.
Multisite trials where appropriate, with shared eligibility criteria and standardized assessments.
Independent methodological approaches to test the robustness of findings.
Preregistered hypotheses, statistical analysis plans and transparent reporting of positive, negative and inconclusive results.
Cross-institutional evidence synthesis, including assessment of heterogeneity and reproducibility.
Shared protocols, analytical specifications and aggregate results should be openly available where feasible. Individual participant data must remain subject to consent, ethics approval, privacy requirements and appropriate data governance. Each institution retains scientific independence and responsibility for regulatory compliance.
Broader research agenda
Cannabinoid pharmacology
Individual cannabinoids and interactions.
Terpene pharmacology
Compound-specific effects.

Chemical composition rather than strain labels.
Drug interactions
Interactions with prescription medications.

Cognition and everyday functioning.
Therapeutic applications

Product standardization
Consistency and reproducibility.
Research accessibility
Access to standardized materials for qualified investigators.
Clinical education
Accessible evidence summaries for patients and clinicians.
These are proposed research directions, not active studies or clinical recommendations.
Research accessibility and clinical education

Clearly distinguish established evidence from preliminary findings and speculation. Evidence summaries should support shared decision-making, not replace clinical care.
Research advocacy only. Cannabis is not an established PTSD treatment; discuss care with a qualified clinician.
